statement: Points A and B are on the same side of a straight river, 3 km and 5 km from it. The points on the bank nearest to A and to B are 6 km apart. A walker goes from A to the river, then on to B. What is the shortest possible length of the walk, in km?

choices.misconception: I reflected B in the river, but then used the difference of the distances, 5 - 3 = 2, instead of their sum.
I added the two distances to the river, 3 + 5, as if the walk could ignore the 6 km along the bank.
I walked straight to the river first, then from that point straight to B, which is not the best point on the bank.
I walked straight to the river, 6 km along the bank, then straight up to B.

hints: Draw it, then think about what a mirror would do to B.
Reflect B in the river. Any route from A to the river to B has the same length as a route from A to the river to the reflected point, and the shortest of those is a straight line.
The reflection of B is 5 km on the other side of the river, so it is 3 + 5 = 8 km across from A and 6 km along.

solutions.reliable: Reflect B in the river to a point B' that is 5 km beyond the bank. For any point P on the bank, PB = PB', so the walk A to P to B has the same length as A to P to B'. That is shortest when A, P and B' lie on a straight line. A and B' are 3 + 5 = 8 km apart across the river and 6 km apart along it, so the distance is the square root of 8² + 6² = 100, which is 10 km. The transferable idea: a path that must touch a line becomes a straight line after reflecting one end in that line.

whyOnTest: Shortest paths that must touch a line are solved by reflection, and the choices include the walker who goes straight to the bank first.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
